written.description: Rules on whether an agent skill is malicious, with a model judge whose catch and false-positive rates are published against a labelled test set. A team picks a policy and suppresses known findings, so the same skill gets the same verdict on every run.

alive.last_commit_message:
fix(llm): send the same LLM prompt for the same skill under every preset (#283)

* fix(llm): send the same prompt for the same skill under every preset

The LLM's severity and title for the same issue moved between rescans, and
moved with the preset: strict rated one issue lower than balanced and
permissive did. Two parts of the prompt changed for reasons unrelated to the
skill.

The untrusted-content delimiter was a fresh random token on every scan, so
no two scans sent the same prompt. It is now a SHA-256 of the wrapped
content. Content cannot carry its own delimiter, because the delimiter is a
hash of the text that would have to contain it.

The structured pre-scan context listed every static finding, including LOW
and INFO package-hygiene findings whose thresholds are preset knobs. Strict's
512-character description limit, for example, added a LOW
MANIFEST_DESCRIPTION_TOO_LONG lead that only strict scans sent. The context
now carries MEDIUM and higher findings only. Reported findings do not change.

* fix(policy): give every preset the same LLM context budgets

Strict gave the LLM smaller content budgets than balanced and permissive
gave it larger ones, so on large skills strict read the least. A budget does
not change what is reported; it only limits what the model sees, and content
over it is excerpted or skipped with an INFO note. Strict and permissive now
use the default budgets, as low-noise and quiet already do, so a preset
changes which findings are reported rather than how much of the skill the
LLM reads.
